pages.title: Introduction
pages.text: Le travail du verre représente le processus de transformation de sable en verre. Pour commencer, vous devez créer l'un des 4 types de $(thing)Mélange verrier$() :$(br)$(br) 1. $(thing)Siliceux$(), de sable blanc.$(br) 2. $(thing)Hématitique$(), de sable jaune, rouge, ou rose.$(br) 3. $(thing)Olivine$(), de sable vert ou brun.$(br) 4. $(thing)Volcanique$(), de sable noir.

Glass batches can then be crafted using one of the aforementioned colors of sand, plus $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#lime_and_potash)Lime$() and a type of $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#lime_and_potash)Potash$().$(br)Remember that different sand types can be obtained by breaking gravel with a hammer.
pages.title: Mélange verrier siliceux
Lime & Potash
pages.text: $(item)Soda Ash$() or $(item)Saltpeter$() can be used as a source of $(thing)Potash$(). Soda ash is a powder made from heating $(thing)Dried Seaweed$() or $(thing)Kelp$().$(br2)$(item)Lime$() is produced by heating $(item)Flux$().

Glassworking is done by starting with a glass batch, and then completing a series of steps. These steps may require specific tools:$(br)$(li)A $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#blowpipe)Blowpipe$(), to $(thing)Blow$() and $(thing)Stretch$().$(li)A $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#paddle)Paddle$(), to $(thing)Flatten$().$(li)$(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#jacks)Jacks$(), to $(thing)Pinch$().$(li)A $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#saw)Gem Saw$(), to $(thing)Saw$().$(li)And a $(l:agriculture/weaving)Wool Cloth$(), to $(thing)Roll$().
pages.title: Outils du métier
Canne de verrier
pages.text: The most important tool is the $(thing)Blowpipe$(). An $(item)Unfired Ceramic Blowpipe$() can be $(thing)knapped$() from clay, and then fired into a $(thing)Ceramic Blowpipe$().$(br)However, ceramic blowpipes are brittle, and have a chance to break when used. An invulnerable $(item)Blowpipe$() can be $(l:craftsmanship/anvils#working)Worked$() from a $(thing)Brass Rod$() on an anvil.

pages.title: Palette
pages.text: L'opération $(thing)Aplatir$() s'effectue à l'aide d'une $(thing)Palette$(), fabriquée à partir de bois.

pages.title: Jacks
pages.text: The $(thing)Pinch$() operation can be done with $(thing)Jacks$(), made from $(l:craftsmanship/anvils#welding)Welding$() a brass rod with a brass plate.

pages.title: Scie à gemme
pages.text: The $(thing)Saw$() operation can be done with a $(item)Gem Saw$(). The gem saw is also used to break both $(item)Glass Blocks$() and $(item)Glass Panes$() to obtain them.

First, glass on the blowpipe must be heated to at least $(4)$(bold)Faint Red$(). Then, hold the blowpipe in your $(thing)offhand$() and hold $(item)$(k:key.use)$() to perform each step$().$(br)Use $(item)$(k:key.swapOffhand)$() to pick up a hot blowpipe into your offhand.$(br2)$(bold)Blow$()$(br)Use the $(thing)Blowpipe$() while facing straight ahead.$(br2)$(bold)Stretch$()$(br)Use the $(thing)Blowpipe$() while facing straight down.
pages.title: How to Work Glass

pages.text: $(bold)Flatten$()$(br)Use the $(thing)Blowpipe$() while holding a $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#paddle)Paddle$() in your main hand.$(br2)$(bold)Pinch$()$(br)Use the $(thing)Blowpipe$() while holding $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#jacks)Jacks$() in your main hand.$(br2)$(bold)Saw$()$(br)Use the $(thing)Blowpipe$() while holding a $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#saw)Gem Saw$() in your main hand.$(br2)$(bold)Roll$()$(br)Use the $(thing)Blowpipe$() with a $(l:agriculture/weaving)Wool Cloth$() in your main hand.
$(bold)Tutorial Slideshow:$() Step by step, creating reinforced glass panes.
$(bold)Tutorial Slideshow:$() Step by step, creating a lens.
$(bold)Tutorial Slideshow:$() Step by step, creating green stained glass.

$(thing)Glass Panes$() are made with a $(thing)Table Pour$(). A pouring table is made by placing up to sixteen $(thing)Kaolin Clay Blocks$() or $(thing)Brass Plated Blocks$() in a continuous area.$(br2) 1. Add a $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking)Glass Batch$() to a $(thing)Blowpipe$().$(br) 2. Heat the blowpipe to $(4)$(bold)Faint Red$().$(br) 3. $()$(item)$(k:key.use)$() the $(thing)Blowpipe$() on the top of the table.$(br) 4. Finally, $(item)$(k:key.use)$() with a $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#paddle)Paddle$() to flatten the glass.
pages.title: Versement sur table

pages.text: Once the glass is cooled, it can be broken with a $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#saw)Gem Saw$() to obtain.

$(thing)Glass Blocks$() are made with a $(thing)Basin Pour$(). A basin is made by surrounding all sides of an air block except the top with $(thing)Kaolin Clay Blocks$() or $(thing)Brass Plated Blocks$().$(br2) 1. Add a $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking)Glass Batch$() to a $(thing)Blowpipe$().$(br) 2. Heat the blowpipe to $(4)$(bold)Faint Red$().$(br) 3. $(item)$(k:key.use)$() the $(thing)Blowpipe$() on the top of the table.
pages.title: Versement en bassin

pages.text: Once the glass is cooled, it can be broken with a $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#saw)Gem Saw$() to obtain.

Glass has a natural color based on the type of $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking)Glass Batch$() that was used. Other colors can be made using a $(l:cooking/bowls#powder_bowl)Bowl$().$(br2)To use, place the $(l:cooking/bowls)Bowl$() on the ground, then $(item)$(k:key.use)$() the required $(thing)Powder$(). Before $(thing)Pouring$(), use the $(thing)Blowpipe$() on the bowl to add the powder to the batch.
